producing_agent.identity: Claude Fable 5 (Cursor agent, under J. Brown direction)

hypothesis: Gate 1 of the essay 'Intention Is All You Need' (the dividend gate) holds at the kernel: on the sixteen worlds {0,1}^4 the choice dividend of a task (D12: best compliant value minus the uniform-compiler expectation over the region) is zero exactly where compliance leaves no slack and positive exactly where the region is wide and the value varies on it. Registered predictions: singleton regions {5} and {12} with U(x) = x have dividend 0 with every best-of-k gain 0; the wide-flat task (all odd worlds, U constant 5) has dividend 0 with all gains <= 0 closing at 0; the wide-varying tasks have dividend exactly 7 (all even worlds, U(x) = x) and exactly 73/11 (popcount >= 2 worlds, U(x) = popcount(x) * 4 - (x % 3)) with weakly increasing gain curves ending exactly at the dividend. gain(1) under the registered ascending scan is deterministic first-element and may be negative (-7 and -15/11 on the wide tasks); the registered claim is about the curve's endpoint and monotonicity, not gain(1) >= 0.
decision: Accept dividend_confirmed if all three gate families hold (DIV_SINGLETON_ZERO, DIV_FLAT_ZERO, DIV_WIDE_POSITIVE). Accept dividend_refuted if any zero-case shows a positive dividend or a wide curve fails to reach its dividend. Otherwise inconclusive. Any recorded verdict passes CI.

gates.DIV_SINGLETON_ZERO: Both singleton tasks: dividend = 0 and every gain(k) = 0.
gates.DIV_FLAT_ZERO: Flat task: dividend = 0, all gains <= 0, gain(region size) = 0.
gates.DIV_WIDE_POSITIVE: Both varying tasks: dividend > 0 matching the registered exact value (7 and 73/11), gain(k) weakly increasing in k, gain(region size) = dividend exactly.
gates.DIV_EXACT_ARITHMETIC: Fractions only; every value, expectation, dividend, and gain serializes exactly.
gates.DIV_RANKING_RECORDED: Verdict is one of the three registered outcomes.
gates.DIV_CLAIM_BOUNDARY: Kernel arithmetic of P11/D12 only; the learner half of Gate 1 — real capability sweeps on real models — is explicitly NOT run here and stays open.

kill_criteria.DIV_SINGLETON_ZERO: The no-slack claim dies if a singleton task shows a nonzero dividend or any nonzero gain.
kill_criteria.DIV_FLAT_ZERO: The flat-value claim dies if the odd-flat task shows a nonzero dividend or a positive gain.
kill_criteria.DIV_WIDE_POSITIVE: The slack-pays claim dies if a wide-varying dividend is not exactly the registered value, the gain curve is not weakly increasing, or the endpoint misses the dividend.
kill_criteria.tuning: Kill the instrument if regions, value rules, scan order, or expected dividends are changed after seeing the curves.

audit_card.target_object: The essay's Gate 1 (dividend gate) at the kernel: is the choice dividend zero exactly on no-slack tasks (singleton or value-flat regions) and positive exactly on wide varying regions, with the best-of-k capability sweep reaching the dividend at full capability?
audit_card.decision: dividend_confirmed / dividend_refuted / inconclusive by the registered rule.
audit_card.representation: Worlds {0,1}^4 encoded 0..15. A task is a registered compliant region in ascending order plus a registered value rule mapping worlds to Fractions. Dividend per D12: max U over the region minus the uniform expectation. Best-of-k selector: max U among the first k elements of the registered scan.
audit_card.data_clock: The capability index k = 1..|region| of the registered ascending scan. No sampling, no RNG, no learning, no LLM.
material_assumptions: The five tasks are the registered literal table: {5} and {12} with U(x) = x; even worlds with U(x) = x; popcount >= 2 worlds with U(x) = popcount(x) * 4 - (x % 3); odd worlds with U constant 5.
The compiler baseline is uniform over the compliant region.
The selector is best-of-k under the registered ascending scan and nothing else.
Expected dividends (0, 0, 7, 73/11, 0) were derived before the run.

objects.task: a pair (R, U) of a nonempty region R subset of W in ascending order and a value function U: R -> Q
objects.dividend: D12: div(R, U) = max_{x in R} U(x) - (1/|R|) * sum_{x in R} U(x)
objects.gain_curve: gain(k) = max of U over the first k elements of the ascending scan, minus the uniform expectation, for k = 1..|R|

mathematical_claim.types_domains_units: Worlds are integers 0..15. Values, expectations, dividends, and gains are exact rationals. Region sizes are 1, 8, 11, and 8. Capability indices k are integers 1..|R|.
mathematical_claim.exact_claim: Singletons: |R| = 1 forces max = mean, so div = 0 and gain(1) = 0; this holds for {5} (U = 5) and {12} (U = 12). Even worlds, U(x) = x: mean = (0+2+...+14)/8 = 7, max = 14, div = 7; the ascending scan gives gains (-7, -5, -3, -1, 1, 3, 5, 7), weakly increasing with endpoint 7. Popcount >= 2 worlds (3,5,6,7,9,10,11,12,13,14,15), U(x) = popcount(x)*4 - (x % 3) with values (8,6,8,11,8,7,10,8,11,10,16): mean = 103/11, max = 16 at x = 15, div = 73/11; gains are (-15/11 x3, 18/11 x7, 73/11), weakly increasing with endpoint 73/11. Odd worlds, U constant 5: max = mean = 5, div = 0, every gain 0. In general div(R, U) = 0 iff U is constant on R (which |R| = 1 forces), and the ascending-scan gain curve is weakly increasing with gain(|R|) = div because the prefix maximum is monotone and reaches the region maximum at k = |R|.
mathematical_claim.quantifiers: Universal over the five registered tasks and over every capability index k within each task (1 + 1 + 8 + 11 + 8 = 29 gain cells). Existential witnesses for negative first gains: gain(1) = -7 on even_worlds and -15/11 on popcount_ge2.
mathematical_claim.assumptions: The registered task table, the uniform compiler baseline, and the ascending-scan best-of-k selector; no other selector, region, or value rule.
mathematical_claim.identification_conditions: Every reported number is a closed-form rational in the registered table; the instrument adds no degrees of freedom, so the zero/positive dichotomy and the curve facts are theorems of D12, not fits.
mathematical_claim.derivation_dependencies: D12 (the dividend definition) and P11 / Theorem-B framing from the essay 'Intention Is All You Need': choice pays exactly the dividend, and the dividend is positive iff compliance leaves value-varying slack.
mathematical_claim.coordinate_invariance: The dividend is invariant under any permutation of the region (max and mean are symmetric); the gain curve is scan-order-dependent by construction, which is why the scan order is registered.
mathematical_claim.edge_limiting_null_cases: Singleton regions are the degenerate no-slack limit (max = mean by arity). The flat task is the wide no-slack limit (max = mean by constancy). gain(1) is deterministic first-element and negative whenever the scan's first value sits below the mean (-7 and -15/11 here); the registered claim constrains the endpoint and monotonicity, not gain(1). A region of size 0 is excluded by construction. The k = |R| endpoint equals the dividend identically — the sweep's last cell is D12 evaluated by scan; recording both is the internal consistency check.

compute.sampling: None. Exact rational evaluation of five registered tasks (29 best-of-k cells) on sixteen worlds.

claim_boundary: Accepted only as: on the five registered tasks over {0,1}^4, the choice dividend of D12 is exactly 0 on both singletons and on the flat wide region, exactly 7 and 73/11 on the two varying wide regions, and the registered best-of-k sweep is weakly increasing with endpoint exactly the dividend. This is the kernel arithmetic of P11/D12 with the Theorem-B framing: intelligence pays only on slack. The learner half of Gate 1 — real capability sweeps on real models — is explicitly NOT run here and stays open. No LLM, no valence, no claim about any real delegate.
